package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is a phishing kit designed to impersonate the official India Post website, collect sensitive user information (PII and payment card data), and facilitate financial fraud. It uses cloned web pages, deceptive payment forms, and exfiltrates data to threat actors.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user visits the phishing page, the code presents a form requesting name, address, email, and phone number, then submits this data to the attacker's backend, enabling PII exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate postal services do not request full PII via unsolicited web forms linked from messages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal India Post sites do not ask for sensitive PII in this context; this is a clear data harvesting attempt.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate e-commerce or government portals may collect PII, but only after secure authentication and with clear context.
key_indicators: Form fields for full address, email, and phone

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user proceeds to the payment page, the code presents a form requesting cardholder name, card number, expiration date, and CVV, then submits this data to the attacker's backend, enabling payment card data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requesting full card details for a minor fee is a classic phishing tactic; legitimate services use secure payment gateways.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal India Post payment flows redirect to trusted payment processors and never request CVV directly on a non-official site.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment forms exist, but only on trusted, verified domains with secure payment processors.
key_indicators: Request for full card details including CVV
No integration with trusted payment gateway
Hosted on a suspicious, lookalike domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon form submission, the code sends collected PII and card data to an attacker-controlled endpoint via HTTP POST, enabling real-time exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to an external, non-India Post endpoint is a hallmark of phishing kits.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate sites process payments and PII internally or via trusted third parties, not via arbitrary POST requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may POST data to their own backend, but not to untrusted, non-affiliated domains.
key_indicators: No visible payment processing or confirmation

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing iMessage with a short URL claiming a package is waiting at India Post.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim clicks the link and visits the phishing site.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site clones the India Post interface and requests PII (name, address, email, phone).
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim submits PII, proceeds to payment page.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site requests payment card details under the pretense of a small redelivery fee.
All collected data (PII and card info) is exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives data for financial fraud or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Web forms on non-official domains requesting PII and full card details
Cloned government or postal service branding on suspicious domains
Immediate exfiltration of form data to external endpoints
file_indicators: HTML forms requesting name, address, email, phone, card number, CVV
JavaScript code making POST requests to non-affiliated domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web traffic to known phishing domains and IPs, especially those mimicking India Post. Flag web forms on non-official domains that request both PII and payment card data. Detect JavaScript or HTML forms that POST sensitive data to external, non-India Post endpoints. Use threat intelligence feeds to block access to newly registered, lookalike domains and monitor for spikes in such registrations.
